messages:
marta (sec-eng): heads-up — noticed a viewer user could see and click the "Run job" button in the Console on a staging workspace. thought we gated that via RBAC. :eyes:
jun (eng-platform): hmm. that should be server-authorized. is this from the recent role-matrix compacting deploy?
devin (sec-eng): likely. i remember we collapsed some implicit perms to reduce rows; might have accidentally given viewer a thin alias that includes jobs.run in the backend mapping.
alex (product): users reported seeing the button but get a 403 when they submit. UX wise that's bad. can we hide it client-side until server check confirms?
jen (sre): there was a failed migration logged during the deploy window: 
ops-bot: deploy rbac-matrix-compact-v2 started by jun at 2026-03-04T18:21Z
ops-bot: migration rbac-matrix-20260304 failed: constraint "role_mapping_unique"
jun (eng-platform): yeah, we retried a manual fix after the constraint hit. i pushed a hotfix that updated the role aliases. maybe alias resolution diverged between console cache and auth API.
qa_lead: reproduced on staging. sequence: login as viewer -> open Jobs list -> Run button visible -> click -> 403 JSON {"error":"permission_denied","required":"jobs.run"}
marta (sec-eng): can we confirm source of truth? auth-api should be canonical. quick check: is console using cached role metadata for rendering buttons?
jun (eng-platform): console keeps a short-lived role cache (30s) for perf. but it calls /auth/v1/permissions before rendering the action menu. theory: cache invalidation race after alias fix.
devin (sec-eng): even so, server must enforce. we should also audit KMS-derived permissions. during onboarding we added an implicit mapping: KMS-key-owner -> editor for resources created with that key. that mapping might be evaluated before the fix and created a transient editor alias.
jen (sre): audit logs show a decrypt event at 2026-03-04T18:23:01 from user viewer-clarice on key key-98b, and the same session shows a jobs.list call. tc: log entries: user_id, session_id present, but missing kms_key_id as a top-level field — makes correlation hard.
alex (product): two asks: 1) hide actions that will 403 at render time to avoid bad UX, 2) ensure audit logs contain kms_key_id and role_resolution snapshot for every auth decision.
marta (sec-eng): agree. short-term: add server-side flag in /auth/v1/permissions response to include resolved_aliases and kms_context_id. that helps Console decide what to render. long-term: tighten alias composition so KMS-based aliasing cannot grant run/create rights by default.
jun (eng-platform): i can open a small PR to make console do a hard-check for sensitive actions: call POST /auth/v1/check with {"action":"jobs.run","resource":"job:%id"} and only render button if allowed. will add exponential backoff for cache miss.
devin (sec-eng): also adding an audit event for the alias resolution step is critical. propose: emit event "rbac.alias_resolved" with fields: principal, resolved_roles (list), source (k/v: kms|assignment|builtin), and migration_tag. we should include kms_key_id when source==kms.
jen (sre): note: logging PII concerns — ensure we redact user email in logs and keep ids. ops-compliance requires user_id + key_id + action.
qa_lead: i'll craft a quick test matrix for staging: viewer/editor/admin permutations + kms-owned resources + cache timings. will verify both button visibility and server 403 behavior.
ops-bot: note: ticket created #SEC-1219 "RBAC alias race: console shows unauthorized actions" assigned to jun, devin, due 2026-03-10
alex (product): timeline? UX patch for hiding -> small, deployable today. server checks + audit events -> needs design review and a small schema migration.
marta (sec-eng): planned steps: 1) jun: quick console guard POST check and hide action (short patch) 2) devin: add alias resolution audit event + include kms_key_id 3) qa_lead: run test matrix on staging 4) jen: validate logs retained in audit store and accessible to compliance 5) followup: review alias composition rules and revert any permissive implicit grants.
jun (eng-platform): starting PR now, will include fallback to show disabled button with tooltip "action not permitted".
devin (sec-eng): i'll draft the audit event schema and feature flag it behind sec.rbac_verbose until we finish retention/cost estimate.
qa_lead: ack, will test when PR hit staging.
marta (sec-eng): thanks. extra note: include correlation_id in client render calls so we can map UI render decisions to audit events.
jen (sre): adding that will help incident triage. tagging oncall: @devops for visibility.
alex (product): :thumbsup: good plan.
